input.reply:
Mara, here are both views side by side. Nothing has been saved yet. You have ₱9,050.00 a month left over after spending and minimum payments.

A (Jun's plan): ₱4,000.00 a month extra on the card and ₱5,050.00 a month into the emergency fund. The card is paid off in 17 months instead of 47 months, and its interest drops from ₱111,635.47 to ₱24,303.62. The emergency fund also reaches its ₱210,000.00 target in 12 months.

B (your plan): all ₱9,050.00 a month on the card. The card is paid off in 9 months (by Jun 15, 2027), and its interest drops to ₱12,460.10. When the card is gone, the same money moves on to the car loan, which is then paid off in 24 months instead of 40 months. The catch is that nothing goes into the emergency fund. It stays at 2.1 months of essential spending, below your 3-month target.

What to weigh: at 3% a month, the card is your most expensive debt, and paying it first fits your avalanche choice. That favours B. But in Session 1 you both said you'd rather have a bigger cash buffer, and that favours A. You and Jun want different things here, so I'm not picking a side. You could also try an amount in between, like ₱6,000 on the card, and I'll run it.

The card is then paid off in 17 months instead of 47, and the emergency fund reaches its ₱210,000.00 target in 12 months, against 7 months if all ₱9,050.00 went to the fund and the card got only its minimum.
